market_context: United States; olive-oil chemistry and international/EU category standards
title: What does olive oil acidity mean?

seo.title: What does olive oil acidity mean?
seo.meta_description: Olive-oil acidity measures free fatty acids expressed as oleic acid, not pH or sour taste. Extra-virgin olive oil is limited to 0.8 g per 100 g under international and EU category standards.
seo.search_intent: Explain free acidity in olive oil, how it is expressed and why it is a chemical quality parameter rather than a flavor score.

excerpt: Olive-oil acidity is a laboratory measure of free fatty acids, conventionally expressed as grams of oleic acid per 100 g of oil. It is not pH and it does not directly measure sourness. Under international and EU standards, extra-virgin olive oil has a maximum free acidity of 0.8 g/100 g; virgin olive oil can be up to 2 g/100 g.
content_html:
A bottle labeled with very low acidity may sound as if it should taste less sharp. That is a common misunderstanding. Olive-oil acidity is a chemical measure of free fatty acids, not a direct measure of flavor intensity.

What the lab is measuring

Most oil fat is stored as triglycerides—fatty acids attached to glycerol. Damage to olives and enzymatic breakdown can release some of those fatty acids before or during processing.

Laboratories quantify the free fraction and conventionally express it as grams of oleic acid per 100 g of oil.

Acidity is not pH

pH is an aqueous acid-base measurement. Olive oil does not behave like lemon juice or vinegar, and its free-acidity value is a different analytical concept.

Why 0.8% matters

International and EU category standards limit extra-virgin olive oil to 0.8 g free acidity per 100 g. Virgin olive oil can have up to 2 g/100 g.

Meeting the acidity limit alone does not make an oil extra virgin. Other chemical criteria and sensory requirements also have to be met.

What higher free acidity can indicate

Free fatty acids can increase when olives are damaged, overripe, poorly stored or processed too slowly. That makes acidity one useful indicator of fruit condition and handling before extraction.

Lower is not automatically tastier

Two extra-virgin oils with free-acidity values of 0.2 and 0.6 g/100 g can both be excellent and taste completely different. Free acidity helps classify chemical quality; it does not predict fruitiness, bitterness, pungency or aroma intensity.

faq.question: What does 0.8% acidity mean in olive oil?
faq.answer: It means up to 0.8 g of free acidity expressed as oleic acid per 100 g of oil, the maximum for extra virgin under international/EU standards.

faq.question: Is olive-oil acidity the same as pH?
faq.answer: No. Free acidity measures free fatty acids; pH is a different measurement used for aqueous systems.

faq.question: Is lower acidity always better?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Low acidity is one positive chemical parameter, but extra-virgin classification also depends on other chemistry and sensory quality.
